newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Nov 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Twenty-four-year-old world superbike champion Troy Corser has confirmed that a factory-prepared Yamaha YZR500 will be his choice of mount when he contests next year's 500cc world motorcycle championship. Page 24.

Australian cricketer Shane Warne said yesterday the Sydney Cricket Ground's reputation as Australia's most spinner-friendly wicket was a myth, a theory which is supported by the fact that in five Tests at the SCG over the past five years he is yet to play in a winning side. Page 24.

On the eve of the fourth Greg Norman Holden Classic, the Shark has admitted his desire to win golf's grand slam - all four major golf tournaments in the one season - and believes it possible, claiming he always knew his best golf would be played when he was in his 40s because of what he learned in his 20s and 30s. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New national soccer coach Terry Venables intends to test Australia's European-based players commitment to the game when he asks them to return to the Socceroos to take part in a four-nation tournament in Australia. Page 47.

Sydney officials for the 2000 Olympics are expected to stick by their ceiling of 10,200 athletes for the Games after it was revealed that several hundred accredited and registered athletes failed to compete at the Atlanta Olympics earlier this year. Page 6.

Australian basketball league veteran and Olympic starting guard Shane Heal's six weeks in the American National Basketball Association has seen him improve his defensive skills and a develop a better passing touch. Page 46.
THE AGE

Jockey Greg Hall narrowly escaped injury in a race fall yesterday after knocking down three of the uprights when he and his mount Malice hit the running rail at the 400-metre mark in the Redleva Handicap at Moonee Valley. Page B8.

The Australian Cricket Board has labelled as inadequate a proposal for a world championship of Test cricket. ACB chief executive Graham Halbish said that although a formal position had not yet been established, the proposal by Wisden editor Matthew Engel as been met with resistance. Page B6.

The reliability of new drug-testing equipment purchased by the Australian Government for the Sydney Olympics has been questioned by the International Olympic Committee who said there had been four positive results from the Atlanta Olympics, previously unannounced because of doubts about the reliability of the testing procedures. Page B6.
HERALD SUN
The world's most famous soccer club, AC Milan, is to send a scout to Australia to talk to the Melbourne Knight's teenage sensation, Joe Simunic, valued at A$1 million by the Knights. Page 94.

Aspiring Australian tennis player Annabel Ellwood was on hand yesterday at Melbourne Park's Davis Cup Room to help launch the Tennis Australia Summer Circuit which will see A$12 million in prize money on offer for seven tournaments. Page 84.

Yesterday's Moonee Valley winner, El Cordobes, will hopefully stay at Brett Mallyon's Cranbourne stables, however a part-ownership with Mick Kent, now training in Singapore, may see the young horse recruited to Singapore. Page 85.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Cricketer Michael Slater has been dropped from the Australian Cricket Team this summer and relegated to play for New South Wales in Sheffield Shield cricket to find form, finding comfort in the fact every senior batsman in the Test side has been similarly dropped and all returned better players. Page 88.
Sprinter Melinda Gainsford is trying hard to regain full fitness by using boxing as the core of her basic conditioning training in an attempt to fight back from her year of injuries. Page 86.

The coveted title of outstanding individual performer at the Atlanta Paralympics has been awarded to Sydney's wheelchair basketball star Troy Sachs, after spearheading his team's gold medal win this year. Page 86.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
